0: Knights by Minoru Murao (DMP) is a dark medieval fantasy adventure. In a land where the church burns suspected witches, the masked squire Mist, feared and hated by villagers as the Black Knight, works against the Saints behind the witch hunts. He travels with Euphemia, a young girl with a gift for brewing potions and poisons. It's a moody, action-driven read for fans of sword-and-sorcery with a grim edge.
2: Märchen by Hayate Kuku (Seven Seas) is a fantasy Boys' Love story built around a magical contract. An enchanted coat seals Sakim, the Divine Beast of the Moon, inside its magic circle, and when the summoner Gil inherits it, he gains command of Sakim. The pair set off together through wolf-filled forests, haunted towns, and bogs of the dead. It suits readers who like their romance wrapped in a dark fairy-tale journey.
3: Magika: Swordsman and Summoner by Mitsuki Mihara (Seven Seas) is a magic-school fantasy with plenty of action and comedy. Humanity has learned to call mythical beings from a parallel dimension, and fifteen-year-old Kazuki Hayashizaki becomes the first male summoner ever, enrolling at a school that has only ever admitted women. His sister, a magic swordswoman sworn to protect summoners, is dead set against it. It's a fit for fans of harem-flavored academy fantasy.
4: Cheeky Brat by Miyuki Mitsubachi (Yen Press) is a sweet, funny high school romance. Yuki Machida, the cool-headed manager of the basketball team, has spent years helping raise her five younger siblings and keeps her own feelings tucked away. She has a crush on the team captain, but a teasing underclassman, Sho Naruse, won't stop pursuing her. It's a warm pick for readers who love push-and-pull romances with a grounded heroine.
5: Dragon Hunter by Hong Seock Seo (Tokyopop) is a Korean fantasy action series steeped in folklore. In an ancient Korea terrorized by dragons, money-hungry hunter Seur Chong takes on the beasts with help from shamans, all while trying to live up to the legend of the great hunter Andrew Yi. Afflicted by the Dragon's Curse, he has to slay a blue dragon if he wants to survive. Expect brawling monster fights, roguish humor, and a mythic backdrop.
6: Dance in the Vampire Bund: Age of Scarlet Order by Nozomu Tamaki (Seven Seas) is a dark supernatural sequel to the original vampire saga. In a United States gripped by vampire hunts, rumors spread that Mina Tepes will gather American vampires on the West Coast and carry them by ship to the Vampire Bund. But the Bund sank months ago, and Mina is said to be dead. It's for readers who want more gothic intrigue and action from the Bund's world.
7: Free Life Fantasy Online: Immortal Princess by Akisuzu Nenohi (Seven Seas) is a relaxed, funny VRMMO fantasy light novel. Gamer Kotone Tsukishiro gets a copy of Free Life Fantasy Online from her younger sister and picks one of its hardest inhuman races to play: a zombie. Her very first quest pulls her into a world that soon becomes a big part of her real life. It's a cozy pick for readers who enjoy game-world stories with an offbeat hero.
8: Phantom Busters by Neoshoco (Viz Media) is a lively supernatural comedy set at a high school. Top student Eugene Korekishi doesn't believe in ghosts, but his classmate Mogari Shishikuro is an exorcist who eats them. Since Mogari can't actually see ghosts himself, the two need someone with the sight, so they start a school exorcist club. It's a fun fit for fans of spooky buddy comedies with plenty of energy.
10: Yakuza Reincarnation by Takeshi Natsuhara and Hiroki Miyashita (Seven Seas) is a rowdy isekai action series with a tough-guy heart. An old-school yakuza is killed by young thugs while defending his turf and wakes up in a fantasy world as a young princess, Sanaria Ryu Lundberg, with his tattoo and strength intact. Now he may be the only one who can teach this world what yakuza honor means. It's great for readers who like brawls, gruff humor, and a fish-out-of-water lead.
12: Pastel by Toshihiko Kobayashi (Del Rey) is a gentle, comedic teen romance. After getting dumped, high schooler Mugi Mugimaru meets Yuu Tsukishima during a summer away and falls for her hard, only to find that she ends up living under the same roof as him. Their awkward closeness sets up plenty of misunderstandings and sweet moments. It's a good pick for fans of classic slice-of-life love stories with a soft, summery feel.
16: Pokémon: Sword & Shield by Hidenori Kusaka and Satoshi Yamamoto (Viz Media) is a bright, kid-friendly adventure based on the Galar region video games. Casey Shield, a hacker who invented the Dynamax Simulator, wants to reunite with a lost Pokémon. Henry Sword, who repairs gear for Pokémon, is searching for the Rusted Sword and Rusted Shield. It's a great pick for young fans of the games and longtime Pokémon Adventures readers.
18: The Strange Adventure of a Broke Mercenary by Mine (Seven Seas) is a grounded sword-and-sorcery light novel. After the mercenaries who raised him die in a bloody battle, Loren is left with only his wits and his sword, so he turns to adventuring. His reckless new party treats him as a meat shield, and only their priest, Lapis, sees what he's worth. It's for readers who like a gruff, practical hero and a partnership that builds over time.
21: Crossplay Love: Otaku x Punk by Toru (Seven Seas) is a playful romantic comedy built on mistaken identities. Gloomy student Yuuma Hanae secretly works at a maid café as "Hana," and his delinquent schoolmate Shuumei Satogiri falls for Hana without knowing who she really is. Shuumei starts visiting the café dressed as a girl named Mei, and soon each is crushing on someone they think is a woman. It's a sweet, silly pick for fans of crossdressing comedies.
